summary:
The Comunitat Valenciana holds a dedicated integral law on the right to identity and gender expression (Llei de 7 d'abril, integral del reconeixement del dret a la identitat i expressió de gènere) alongside a general LGTBI-protection statute, making it one of only three communities (with Andalucía and Madrid) to have enacted legislation in both the trans-specific and general-LGTBI-equality categories. Unlike Madrid, Valencia has not amended or narrowed its provisions. The statutory framework supports institutional response channels for a visitor encountering discrimination.

No incident data, enforcement action, or negative visitor-facing finding was located for this community in the research pass. Valencia city carries a visible and well-established LGBTQ community with dedicated infrastructure. The divergence from national is modest and rests on the statutory-completeness evidence.

Vs national (0.88): +0.03, reflecting the presence of a dual-category legislative framework (gender identity + LGTBI equality) that is active and unrevised. Vs Madrid (0.83), which shares the dual-category structure but actively rolled back its provisions in 2023, Valencia's position is clearly safer. Vs Castilla y León (0.81), which has no law at all, the gap is 0.10 points driven entirely by the presence versus absence of statutory infrastructure.

sources.summary: Trans-rights federation's autonomous-community legislation inventory: lists the Comunitat Valenciana's two regional statutes - Ley 8/2017 (integral law recognising the right to gender identity and expression, 7 April) and Ley 23/2018 (LGTBI persons' equality) - and shows Andalucía (Ley 2/2014 + Ley 8/2017) and Madrid (Ley 2/2016 + Ley 3/2016) as the other communities holding both a trans-specific and a general LGTBI law; the basis for the dual-category claim in the summary.

LGTBI federation's 2025 radiography of public educational policies across Spanish regions: tracks which autonomidades have gender-identity protocols and education legislation; notes the Valencian parliament completing its gender legislation and groups the Comunidad Valenciana with Madrid, Extremadura, Murcia and Navarra among the leaders on educational policy coverage.

localsOnly: The regional identity-and-expression law's registry and administrative procedures operate for residents; a visitor never invokes them.
